admissibility_policy.meaning: admissible means explicit, scoped, and testable or constitutive; it does not mean empirically true
admissibility_policy.empirical_closure_rule: a real-world application requires at least one empirical_study reference and at least one manifest-backed machine check

assumptions.statement: Visited vertices cannot be revisited and the forward feasible set is history dependent.
assumptions.scope: All IDP traversal claims using condition C1.
assumptions.role: Defines endogenous feasibility rather than asserting an empirical frequency.

testability.criterion: An application is outside scope when reversals, recalls, or costless backtracking are feasible.

assumptions.statement: The focal local theorem uses a degree-two start with a terminal trap neighbor.
assumptions.scope: Canonical and five-state local examples, not arbitrary graphs.
assumptions.role: Makes the routing mechanism finite and exactly enumerable.

testability.criterion: The assumption fails when the trap branch has further feasible continuation or the start has additional available neighbors.

assumptions.statement: At the focal degree-two root, selecting either neighbor leads through a forced continuation to a beta-independent terminal payoff; the higher-immediate-reward route has the lower terminal payoff.
assumptions.scope: Publication forms of the greedy-wrongness lemma and central dilemma theorem; deeper or branching continuations use the separate general-tree theorem.
assumptions.role: Turns the graph and stopping process into an exact two-route terminal-reward model without a hand-coded welfare kernel.

testability.criterion: The specialization fails when either selected branch contains an additional signal-dependent routing decision or when the terminal payoff depends on beta.

assumptions.statement: Reward signals are Gaussian and reveal rewards but not the realized percolation topology.
assumptions.scope: Precision-comparative-statics claims using beta.
assumptions.role: Separates reward information from structural knowledge.

testability.criterion: Recompute the claim under non-Gaussian noise and under signals that include edge-state information.

assumptions.statement: Reward-signal errors are independent across vertices and have the common Gaussian variance indexed by beta.
assumptions.scope: Closed-form Gaussian pairwise-routing probabilities, including the within-reachable-set oracle and depth-d trap tree.
assumptions.role: Makes each trap-versus-bridge signal difference Gaussian with variance twice the individual signal variance and separates choices across distinct tree levels.

testability.criterion: Recompute route probabilities and path-success dependence under correlated or heteroskedastic reward errors.

assumptions.statement: The greedy agent ranks currently available neighbors by posterior immediate reward rather than continuation value.
assumptions.scope: Greedy-agent welfare reversal claims only.
assumptions.role: Defines the misspecified objective that can create the reversal.

testability.criterion: Choice data can compare immediate-reward rankings with continuation-value rankings at otherwise matched decision nodes.

assumptions.statement: Vertex rewards are independent Uniform[0,1] draws where closed-form order statistics are used.
assumptions.scope: Cluster-size welfare formulas and local trap prevalence calculations.
assumptions.role: Provides exact order-statistic and ranking-reversal probabilities.

testability.criterion: Replace the reward law and recompute order statistics; no empirical universality is asserted.

assumptions.statement: Edges are blocked independently with common probability p.
assumptions.scope: Lattice, Erdos-Renyi thinning, and configuration-model percolation claims.
assumptions.role: Matches the independent bond-percolation theorems used as external premises.

testability.criterion: Correlated or targeted failures require a separate model and are outside the cited threshold formulas.

assumptions.statement: For each fixed blocking probability p above the lattice threshold, the expected reachable-set size is bounded by a finite constant C_p uniformly over the finite network sequence.
assumptions.scope: The uniform-in-network form of the informational-decay proposition only.
assumptions.role: States the exact finite-volume first-moment input needed to aggregate the kernel-proved conditional Gaussian oracle regret bound.

testability.criterion: Verify a uniform cluster-size first-moment bound for the chosen finite graph sequence; otherwise retain only the per-network conditional regret inequality.

assumptions.statement: The reachable-set-size law assigns probability at least rho > 0 to singleton reachable sets uniformly along the finite network sequence.
assumptions.scope: The unconditional constant-order half of the repaired topological-loss proposition only.
assumptions.role: Separates persistent local fragmentation from giant-component membership and supplies the exact lower-bound input used by the finite-law aggregation theorem.

testability.criterion: Compute or bound the singleton reachable-set probability for the specified graph and failure law; without a uniform positive bound retain only the conditional cluster-size formula.

assumptions.statement: A scalar kappa interpolates between immediate-reward and continuation-value objectives.
assumptions.scope: Cognitive-threshold and kappa comparative-statics claims.
assumptions.role: Defines a one-dimensional reduced-form cognition family.

testability.criterion: Estimate kappa from repeated routing choices and report sensitivity to alternative interpolation rules.

assumptions.statement: The depth-d continuation estimator has constants 0 < c2 <= c1 independent of depth, accepts a bridge whenever topology-noise variance is at most c2, and rejects it whenever variance exceeds c1; behavior inside the band is unrestricted.
assumptions.scope: Part 5 of the depth-d error-compounding proposition only.
assumptions.role: Defines the reduced-form semantic response required to convert the topology-noise formula into lower and upper cognitive-depth thresholds.

testability.criterion: For any specified posterior estimator, verify depth-uniform acceptance and rejection constants or replace the proposition with estimator-specific thresholds.

assumptions.statement: On the five-state benchmark, a structurally aware agent observes the bridge state with probability 1 - 2^(-kappa) and otherwise observes an erasure; revealed and erased signals use the explicit routing rule in Proposition prop:threshold-five-state.
assumptions.scope: Only the finite five-state cognition and reward-precision propositions; it does not identify the Gaussian topology signal or the depth-d trap-tree model.
assumptions.role: Provides a fully specified Blackwell-ordered finite experiment whose routing and welfare are exactly machine checkable.

testability.criterion: Recompute the finite theorem under alternative reveal functions or non-erasure signal alphabets; do not transfer the endpoint formulas without re-proving them.

assumptions.statement: A scalar alpha weights instrumental reward relative to an independent sentimental component.
assumptions.scope: Alpha-threshold and sentimental-immunity claims.
assumptions.role: Defines the paper's non-instrumental preference perturbation.

testability.criterion: Calibrate alpha from choices with independently varied monetary and sentimental attributes and test alternative dependence structures.

assumptions.statement: Population welfare aggregates individual welfare over a specified distribution of cognitive parameters.
assumptions.scope: Principal and disclosure claims.
assumptions.role: Defines the planner's aggregation problem.

testability.criterion: The parameter distribution must be estimated or supplied, and conclusions must be sensitivity-tested over alternative distributions.

assumptions.statement: The principal theorem uses a finite nonnegatively weighted population, continuous individual welfare, one common tail-dominance threshold, and one witnessed positive aggregate improvement over zero precision.
assumptions.scope: Part 1 of Proposition prop:principal-optimum only; reversal-regime membership by itself is not substituted for these conditions.
assumptions.role: States exactly the regularity and strict-improvement inputs needed for a positive global maximizer on the noncompact precision domain.

testability.criterion: For each proposed population, verify continuity, a common finite tail threshold, and an explicit positive-precision welfare improvement before invoking the interior-optimum conclusion.

assumptions.statement: For matched low- and high-cognition populations, every agent's welfare increment from beta1 to beta2 is weakly larger in the high-cognition population whenever zero <= beta1 <= beta2, and the two aggregate maximizers are unique.
assumptions.scope: Part 2 of Proposition prop:principal-optimum only; no FOSD-only or approximate-noise claim is made.
assumptions.role: Provides the exact finite-increment single-crossing premise from which monotone optimal precision follows.

testability.criterion: Check the four-value increment inequality over the policy interval and verify uniqueness or adopt an explicit extremal-maximizer selection rule.

assumptions.statement: The regime-bifurcation possibility result uses an equal-weight two-type reduced form with equipped welfare beta and reversal-prone welfare max(4 - 4 beta, 0).
assumptions.scope: Part 3 of Proposition prop:principal-optimum only; it is a constructive possibility witness, not an IDP-wide implication of threshold mass.
assumptions.role: Separates the exact existence of a strict aggregate precision valley from unsupported claims that every mixed-threshold population has one.

testability.criterion: The witness establishes possibility only; applications must replace both type-welfare schedules and recheck the three-point inequalities.

assumptions.statement: The Bayesian benchmark observes the realized percolation state before optimizing a traversal strategy.
assumptions.scope: Conditional-reduction, Bayesian-immunity, and information-knowledge complementarity claims.
assumptions.role: Defines the full-structural-knowledge benchmark.

testability.criterion: The benchmark does not apply when the agent observes only a prior over topology.

assumptions.statement: The Bayesian-naive five-state agent routes using a prior-only continuation estimate with perceived blocking probability hat-p.
assumptions.scope: Bayesian-naive five-state proposition only.
assumptions.role: Defines a distinct misspecification from topology omission.

testability.criterion: Routing choices must remain signal independent at the start node and identify the implied prior threshold.

assumptions.statement: For the selected C2-prime trap/bridge pair, the bridge-selection probability is eventually positive and the exact welfare remainder after subtracting the bridge probability times the limiting greedy-path advantage is little-o of that probability.
assumptions.scope: General-tree reversal theorem only.
assumptions.role: Controls the relative tail rates of finite-precision continuation errors and competing root alternatives; bounded convergence alone is insufficient.

testability.criterion: For each proposed graph family, derive or numerically bracket the relevant choice-error exponents and verify the epsilon remainder bound before applying the theorem.

assumptions.statement: The network sequence is an uncorrelated configuration model with a power-law degree law and the regularity conditions required by the cited threshold theorem.
assumptions.scope: Power-law application only; targeted removal and arbitrary empirical networks are excluded.
assumptions.role: States the model class on which moment-based percolation criteria are valid.

testability.criterion: Check degree-law fit, degree correlations, finite-size cutoff, and removal mechanism before applying the threshold formula.
